# Wild Fire (G4)

Wild Fire is the cream-colored, dark-brown-maned Pegasus who gets into a hooficure argument in Canterlot. She is the ponysona of *Friendship Is Magic* storyboard artist Sabrina “Sibsy” Alberghetti, whose character actually made it into the television series. Look for her amber-brown eyes and distinctive flaming-tire cutie mark.

[![Wild Fire and Lucky Clover — Hasbro/DHX Media, A Canterlot Wedding](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/mlp/images/0/06/Lucky_and_Wildfire_arguing_S02E25.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/201?cb=20120422154901)](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Wild_Fire/Gallery)

[![Wild Fire and MandoPony — artwork credited to Sibsy](https://cdn.twibooru.org/img/2020/7/23/2128918/full.png)](https://twibooru.org/2128918)

- **Name and origin:** Fans reportedly named Alberghetti's initially unnamed ponysona Wild Fire, and she adopted the name. The [naming history](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/My_Little_Pony%3A_Friendship_Is_Magic/Characters/Background_Ponies) is secondary reporting; the original naming exchange was not independently recovered. Enterplay's licensed [Speed Racer card](https://data.mlpmerch.com/ccg/details/pfps8/) establishes merchandise usage of the two-word name. The name is not spoken in her debut.
- **Speaking status:** She speaks in her debut, voiced in English by Tabitha St. Germain, not Alberghetti. Her [character reference](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Wild_Fire) also documents her silent appearances in *Wonderbolts Academy* (S3E7) and *Top Bolt* (S6E24), plus IDW comics #1, #7, #9, #11 and #23, among other appearances. Her academy model differs from her original design.
- **Other media:** She is playable in the [Gameloft game](https://mlp-gameloft.fandom.com/wiki/Wild_Fire). The licensed cards characterize her as fast, hot-tempered and artistically talented. Her creator-avatar origin does not make her television appearance fan-only; the creator's separate artwork is not automatically television canon.

## Important moments

1. **The hooficure dispute — A Canterlot Wedding – Part 1 (S2E25).** Wild Fire insists on getting her hooves done despite Lucky Clover's objections, giving this background mare an unusually memorable speaking debut. [Episode transcript](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/A_Canterlot_Wedding_-_Part_1) (timestamp unavailable).
2. **Cadance restores the romance — A Canterlot Wedding – Part 1 (S2E25).** During the same childhood flashback, Cadance casts a spell on the bickering pair and they become affectionate again, illustrating her power to spread love. [Full episode listing](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jIjXL4InWBg) (scene timestamp unavailable).
3. **The double dare — Rainbow Dash and the Daring Do Double Dare (2014 chapter book, not a TV episode).** Wild Fire questions whether Daring Do's exploits are realistic and challenges Rainbow Dash to imitate them, setting the book's central adventure in motion. [Book synopsis](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Rainbow_Dash_and_the_Daring_Do_Double_Dare).

*Verification note:* The original naming exchange, voice actress's original confirmation and full-episode timestamps could not be independently retrieved. Both image URLs are documented by their linked pages, but the image servers blocked direct verification in this session.
